L2t: Bladder washout (irrigation) solutions are typically sterile saline or other prescribed irrigants used to clear catheters or the bladder.
L3t: Irrigating fluid is kept near body temperature or at room temperature, because fluid that is too cold can trigger bladder spasm and chill the patient.
L4t: Bladder washout solution should be at room temperature.
L2f: Bladder washout solutions are always made up fresh from powdered concentrate and mixed with tap water at the bedside.
L3f: Chilled irrigant is preferred for bladder washouts because the cold constricts bleeding vessels and soothes the bladder lining, so fluid is kept refrigerated until use.
L4f: Bladder washout solution should be cold.
